access-keys-rotated.reason: IAM user access keys; the enclave creates no IAM users (roles only). Landing-zone identity baseline (IAM Identity Center).

acm-certificate-expiration-check.reason: No ACM certificates (no load balancers / custom domains).

api-gw-associated-with-waf.reason: No API Gateway; ingress is the AgentCore Runtime/Gateway (JWT, VPC endpoint).

dynamodb-throughput-limit-check.reason: Account throughput vs. limit at runtime; the ledger is on-demand.

ec2-managedinstance-association-complian.reason: No EC2 instances / SSM managed nodes in the enclave.

ec2-managedinstance-patch-compliance-sta.reason: No EC2 instances / SSM managed nodes in the enclave.

elasticache-redis-cluster-automatic-back.reason: ElastiCache is allowed for tenants; the enclave creates no cache.

elasticsearch-encrypted-at-rest.reason: No OpenSearch (excluded by ADR 0001; vector store is Aurora).

encrypted-volumes.reason: No EBS volumes (EBS default encryption is set account-wide anyway).

guardduty-non-archived-findings.reason: Operational: GuardDuty findings must be triaged within the window; the enclave enables GuardDuty (security-services).

iam-group-has-users-check.reason: IAM groups/users are not created by the enclave; identity via IAM Identity Center.

iam-root-access-key-check.reason: Root user hygiene is an account baseline (Control Tower / LZA).

iam-user-group-membership-check.reason: No IAM users in the enclave; identity via IAM Identity Center.

iam-user-mfa-enabled.reason: No IAM users in the enclave; identity via IAM Identity Center (MFA enforced there).

iam-user-no-policies-check.reason: No IAM users in the enclave.

iam-user-unused-credentials-check.reason: No IAM users in the enclave.

kinesis-stream-encrypted.reason: No Kinesis Data Streams (Firehose is allowed for tenants; streams are not).

mfa-enabled-for-iam-console-access.reason: No IAM users in the enclave; console access via IAM Identity Center with MFA.

no-unrestricted-route-to-igw.reason: Customer VPC routing; the enclave requires private subnets without IGW routes.

rds-snapshots-public-prohibited.reason: Snapshots exist only at runtime; Aurora is private, and the snapshot-sharing block is set account-wide (see ebs-snapshot-public-restorable-check for EBS).

restricted-common-ports.reason: Security groups are customer inputs; the sandbox fixture allows only 443/5432 inside the VPC CIDR.

restricted-ssh.reason: Security groups are customer inputs (endpoint / agent / Aurora SGs); the sandbox fixture opens no SSH.

ssm-document-not-public.reason: No SSM documents (account-level SSM document sharing block is a landing-zone setting).

subnet-auto-assign-public-ip-disabled.reason: Customer VPC subnets; the enclave requires private subnets (sandbox fixture complies).

vpc-sg-open-only-to-authorized-ports.reason: Security groups are customer inputs; no 0.0.0.0/0 ingress in the sandbox fixture.

vpc-vpn-2-tunnels-up.reason: Site-to-site VPN (e.g. DoD BCAP path) is customer network; the enclave creates none.

Perform periodic scans of the information system [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and real-time scans of files from external sources at [Selection(one or more); endpoint; network entry/exit points] as the files are downloaded, opened, or executed in accordance with organizational security policy; and 2. [Selection(one or more): block malicious code; quarantine malicious code; send alert to administrator; [Assignment: organization-defined action]] in response to malicious code detection; and d. Addresses the receipt of false positives during malicious code detection and eradication and the resulting potential impact on the availability of the information system. Supplemental Guidance: Information system entry and exit points include, for example, firewalls, electronic mail servers, web servers, proxy servers, remote-access servers, workstations, notebook computers, and mobile devices. Malicious code includes, for example, viruses, worms, Trojan horses, and spyware. Malicious code can also be encoded in various formats(e.g., UUENCODE, Unicode), contained within compressed or hidden files, or hidden in files using steganography. Malicious code can be transported by different means including, for example, web accesses, electronic mail, electronic mail attachments, and portable storage devices. Malicious code insertions occur through the exploitation of information system vulnerabilities. Malicious code protection mechanisms include, for example, anti-virus signature definitions and reputation-based technologies. A variety of technologies and methods exist to limit or eliminate the effects of malicious code. Pervasive configuration management and comprehensive software integrity controls may be effective in preventing execution of unauthorized code. In addition to commercial off-the-shelf software, malicious code may also be present in custom-built software. This could include, for example, logic bombs, back doors, and other types of cyber attacks that could affect organizational missions/business functions. Traditional malicious code protection mechanisms cannot always detect such code. In these situations, organizations rely instead on other safeguards including, for example, secure coding practices, configuration management and control, trusted procurement processes, and monitoring practices to help ensure that software does not perform functions other than the functions intended. Organizations may determine that in response to the detection of malicious code, different actions may be warranted. The SGEA L2 account-baseline guardrail level is an account-enforced guardrail applied to every model invocation.

The enforced guardrail evaluates every user message and tool result, so a caller cannot narrow guarding with guardContent tags. System prompts (developer-authored) are SELECTIVE; whole-system-prompt evaluation trips the prompt-attack filter on ordinary agent instructions.
Guardrail configuration (denied topics, regexes) encrypted with the enclave CMK.
Bedrock Agents session and memory data encrypted with the enclave CMK.
Every agent carries the tenant guardrail (SGEA L3 tenant-enforced level).
Same session-termination bound as SGEA-AC-RT-06.
Knowledge-base ingestion intermediates encrypted with the enclave CMK.
Interface endpoints for bedrock-runtime, bedrock-agent-runtime and bedrock-agentcore keep inference traffic off the internet.
Agent runtimes execute customer code and reach enclave data; PUBLIC mode puts them outside the enclave boundary.
VPC mode must pin private enclave subnets (no IGW route).
Egress must be restricted to enclave VPC endpoints.
Inbound invocation must authenticate end users against the organization IdP so actions are attributable per user (also required by per-user token control).
Execution role scoped to the tenant's resources only; no admin or wildcard actions.
FedRAMP SC-10 parameter is <=15 min for user sessions; idle agent sessions holding user context must terminate within that.
Forward only explicitly allow-listed headers into agent code.
Runtime container images come from a private ECR repo with scanning.
Immutable tags make the deployed agent image traceable to a reviewed build (CM-2/CM-3).
Tool calls must be authenticated; an unauthenticated gateway exposes every target.
Customer-managed key for gateway configuration and stored credentials.

The SGEA gateway_tool_path guardrail level is enforced on tool invocations by the AgentCore policy engine, or (where AWS does not offer it, e.g. GovCloud) by the SGEA tool-policy REQUEST interceptor Lambda.
